scope: Static review of existing release fixture, linked native crypto, canonical provider preparation and identity requirements. No provider installation/substitution, key generation, build, test execution, repository edit or assertion removal by this reviewer.

reported_original_failure.source: Root/native-run owner report; complete raw test output not independently read by this reviewer

reported_current_linked_backend.source: Native-run owner chain_acceptance reported its ROG read-only probe; primary probe result not yet local to this review

fixture_call_chain: Read TRNM_PQ_OPENSSL and TRNM_PQ_OPENSSL_SHA256; hash actual CLI bytes and compare to supplied pin. This proves agreement with the supplied pin, not canonical provider provenance by itself.
Spawn that CLI with genpkey -algorithm ML-DSA-87 or SLH-DSA-SHA2-256s -outform DER; force OPENSSL_CONF=/dev/null for the subprocess.
Parse returned private DER through linked in-process openssl::PKey::private_key_from_der; derive canonical public DER in that same Rust process.
Sign fixture messages for both families in-process using openssl::sign::Signer::new_without_digest and sign_oneshot_to_vec.

Root quorum/possession verification checks linked openssl::version::number >=0x30500000; ML-DSA-87 verification uses the RustCrypto CandidateVerifier, while SLH-DSA-SHA2-256s verification uses in-process OpenSSL PKey/Verifier.

canonical_provider.smoke_scope: CLI ML-DSA-65 real key generation, sign, verify and wrong-message rejection

conclusions: CLI environment variables alone repair only the first fixture precondition. They do not change a static linked backend or relink the already built Rust ELF.

The owner-reported 3.5.5 satisfies the source minimum >=3.5.0; these eleven failures do not prove unsupported algorithms or a failed crypto assertion. Algorithm operation after fixing fixture inputs remains untested in this review.
A 3.5.9 CLI plus the old dynamically linked 3.5.5 Rust backend is a mixed-provider run, not the canonical 3.5.9 static provider binding. Do not promote it by setting environment labels.

Canonical repair requires the verified isolated preparation receipt and compilation under the exported OPENSSL_DIR/OPENSSL_STATIC before producing a new test ELF. An export after compilation cannot prove the previous ELF used that prefix.
The ML-DSA-65 CLI smoke is necessary preparation evidence but does not substitute for the fixture ML-DSA-87 and SLH-DSA-SHA2-256s Rust parsing/signing/verification scenarios.
Runtime OPENSSL_CONF and OPENSSL_MODULES must be observed for the Rust process as well as the CLI. The fixture subprocess-only CONF override does not configure the parent Rust process.

required: Actual source archive SHA equals canonical pin
M5 preparation script SHA
Untouched attempt log and provider.json result/last_stage/exit
Actual CLI version and CLI SHA
Hashes of both headers and libcrypto.a/libssl.a
Smoke outcomes, exported configuration, source transport
Source M5/tree and Cargo.lock identity
Exact package/features/profile/toolchain and Cargo executable
Original compilation environment including OPENSSL_DIR/STATIC and target-specific overrides if present
openssl-sys build-script output and Cargo fingerprint identifying link search/selection
Actual linked static archive identities; absence of a dynamic NEEDED entry alone is not provenance
New compiler-artifact ELF SHA/size tied to this build
Exact test ELF before/after identity
Recorded execution argv, package cwd and relevant provider environment
For a dynamic build, resolved libcrypto/libssl paths and file hashes and version from that exact library; SONAME alone is insufficient
For static canonical build, retained native archive/link evidence plus observable runtime backend identity where available
Actual module configuration and any external provider modules if used
Retain original 56-pass/11-fail attempt and raw failure logs
Separate new attempt for changed build/runtime identity
Execute original relevant test roster and retain actual counts/failed/ignored/filtered scopes
A successful preparation or build is not a native test pass or production qualification

recommended_scope: Finish the already authorized canonical isolated 3.5.9 preparation, preserve its exact provenance, compile under it and retain distinct artifact/runtime identities for the existing tests. This reviewer performs no such execution and does not replace any source guard or assertion.
